title: Stonetalon Mountains
body: The Stonetalon Mountains rise west of the Barrens and south of Ashenvale, a range of forested peaks, deep canyons and mountain lakes, and both tauren and night elves have long held its great peak sacred. In the Third War, Jaina Proudmoore and Thrall each came to the caverns of Stonetalon Peak seeking the Oracle, and there the prophet Medivh urged orc and human to set aside old hatreds and stand together against the Burning Legion. Today the mountains are wounded. The Venture Company is stripping Windshear Crag of its forests, and the fires of its machines left the Charred Vale a blackened ruin of raging elementals and Bloodfury harpies. The spirits of the land cry out in pain, and both the Horde and the night elves have heard them. The Horde holds Sun Rock Retreat and the troll camp of Malaka'jin, while the night elves keep a small outpost on Stonetalon Peak beside the barrow of the Talon Den. Grimtotem tauren prowl the southeastern valleys, spiders haunt the Webwinder Path, and kobolds dig deep beneath Boulderslide Ravine.

title: Greatwood Vale
body: The Greatwood Vale lies in the southeast of the mountains, where the road running west from the Crossroads climbs out of the Barrens. The Horde shaman Seereth Stonebreak keeps her camp near its edge, at the border of the two lands, and from there the way leads on to the northwest toward the logging grounds of Windshear Crag. The vale is not safe. Grimtotem mercenaries and ruffians roam its woods in great numbers, with brutes and sorcerers among them. Close to the troll camp of Malaka'jin, night elves sit caged in the vale as prisoners of the witch doctor Jin'Zil.

title: Malaka'jin
body: Malaka'jin is a small troll camp at the base of the mountains, in the far southeast near the Barrens. Its people live well off the hunting in these hills, though lately spiders have been creeping into the camp by night to steal their kills, and Xen'Zilla wants the beasts thinned. In his cave at the camp, the witch doctor Jin'Zil keeps caged night elves and bubbling cauldrons of his own brews. Ken'zigla prepares healing draughts for wounded Horde soldiers as far off as Camp Taurajo, and Darn Talongrip sends willing recruits north to join the Horde campaign in Ashenvale.

title: Camp Aparaje
body: Camp Aparaje was a small tauren village in the southeastern hills of Stonetalon, home to Makaba Flathoof and his daughter Kaya. The Grimtotem fell upon it, led by Grundig Darkcloud of the post further up the path, and killed nearly everyone. Makaba slew all the raiders he could before he barely escaped with his life, and he now waits on the edge of the mountains by the Barrens, sure his daughter was lost in the attack. Grimtotem ruffians and mercenaries still pick through the abandoned camp. For those who know these trails, though, Aparaje remains a landmark on the road home.

title: Grimtotem Post
body: Grimtotem Post is a camp of the Grimtotem tribe in the southeastern Stonetalon Mountains, a little further up the path beyond Camp Aparaje. Brutes stand guard and sorcerers work their magic here, and the post is commanded by Grundig Darkcloud, who led the brutal raid that destroyed Aparaje, with his own band of brutes close about him. A tauren called Gorehoof the Black roams the camp as well. Not all of Aparaje's people died in that raid. Makaba Flathoof's daughter Kaya was taken alive, and she is held captive at the post, waiting for the chance to slip away.

title: The Webwinder Path
body: The Webwinder Path is the long road that winds north from the southern valleys through the heart of the mountains, toward Sun Rock Retreat and Windshear Crag. It is named well. Deepmoss spiders, creepers and venomspitters, hunt along its length, and travelers who walk it by night risk the fangs of Besseleth, the great spider of nearby Sishir Canyon, whose bounty notice is posted beside the road. On a rise overlooking the valley that leads into Windshear Crag, the night elf Kaela Shadowspear and her gnome companion Gaxim Rustfizzle have made their camp, plotting against the Venture Company.

title: Sishir Canyon
body: Sishir Canyon opens west of the Webwinder Path, and it belongs to the spiders. Besseleth and her eight-legged brood have claimed it as their webbed lair, and the canyon floor is thick with deepmoss creepers, webspinners and venomspitters among clusters of eggs. Besseleth is an old predator of these parts who hunts the road by night, and she once caught Maggran Earthbinder of Sun Rock Retreat with her two-foot fang. A goblin trader in Ratchet pays well for deepmoss eggs, now prized for omelettes in Booty Bay, though even he warns that gathering them in Sishir is not for the weak of stomach.

title: Boulderslide Ravine
body: Southeast of Sun Rock Retreat, Boulderslide Ravine cuts into the mountains, and at its end a deep cavern runs far beneath the stone. The Gogger kobolds have claimed it, rock keepers, geomancers and stonepounders who mine a rare crystal called resonite with frantic haste and shriek at anyone who reaches for their candles. The shaman Mor'rogal found that the crystals carry a trace of earthen magic, and the truth lay at the bottom of the cave: a resonite cask in which an earthen named Goggeroc slumbers. The earthen were made by the titans to shape the land itself, and the kobolds may have dug too deep.

title: Sun Rock Retreat
body: Sun Rock Retreat is the Horde's stronghold in the Stonetalon Mountains, a village of tauren and orcs tucked among the peaks south of Mirkfallon Lake and guarded by Stonetalon grunts. Its leader, the veteran Maggran Earthbinder, was sent here by Cairne Bloodhoof himself. Tammra Windfield calls on the Earthmother to help the scorched land grow again, the shaman Mor'rogal senses something evil stirring beneath the mountains, and Tsunaman serves the Tribunal of the Tides, waging the ancient war of water against fire in the Charred Vale. An inn and a wind rider post serve travelers, and at the edge of the village the mage Braelyn Firehand pursues a darker purpose of her own.

title: Mirkfallon Lake
body: Mirkfallon Lake lies north of Sun Rock Retreat, its shores the home of the Pridewing wyverns. Consorts, skyhunters and soarers nest about the water, a great patriarch among them, and a wyvern called Sorrow Wing hunts the shore. Sources in Theramore claim the orcs gather pridewing venom here for their assassins, and the Sentinels of Astranaar have sent fighters south to deny them the source. The lake also holds gentler gifts. Gaea seeds, found nowhere else in the mountains, lie along the water's edge, and the tauren of Sun Rock gather them in the hope of restoring Stonetalon's lost forests.

title: The Charred Vale
body: The Charred Vale in the southwest of the mountains was once a verdant forest. The Venture Company set it ablaze and turned its machines of destruction upon it, and in doing so loosed raging spirits of flame and stone. The treants of the vale seem to have driven the goblins back, but even these guardians were corrupted, some perhaps by the weapons the goblins used in their retreat, and blackened ancients now lumber through the ash. The Bloodfury harpies have since made the vale their stronghold, barring the druids who would heal it, while scorched basilisks and chimaeras hunt the burned slopes. The road south to Desolace runs through it.

title: Windshear Crag
body: Windshear Crag is a broad valley in the east of the mountains, and it is where the Venture Company's greed is laid bare. Loggers, deforesters and operators swarm a landscape of stumps and fouled water, and the company's lumber mill stands south of Cragpool Lake. Two great shredders marked XT:4 and XT:9 fell trees faster than the spirits can bear, and wagons of explosives wait along the trails. Kobold diggers toil for the company here too, and deepmoss spiders lay their eggs under what trees remain. On the crag's western edge, the goblin Ziz Fizziks, fired when a gnome took charge of the operation, has set up camp and now works against his former employers.

title: Windshear Mine
body: The Windshear Mine sits at the far eastern end of Windshear Crag, where the Blackwolf River ends. The Venture Company works it with kobolds in its employ, diggers, geomancers and overlords. On Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle's orders, large amounts of a strange gold-green ore are being hauled from its depths, for a purpose none of the miners has learned. Among them is Piznik, once the second most important goblin at the site, sent down to the tunnels when Gerenzo took over and now quietly spying for his old boss. The overlords grow wary of him all the same. The company keeps some of its letters here, deep inside.

title: Cragpool Lake
body: Cragpool Lake lies in the north of Windshear Crag, and the Venture Company has crowded its shores. Oil spills slick the water, while engineers, machine smiths and builders keep the company's machines running along the banks, and a goblin named Nizzik sells Venture armor to any customer with coin. Far above the lake, up beside the great water wheel, Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle keeps watch over the entire site from his high platform. From the lake the Blackwolf River runs out through the crag, and travelers bound for Stonetalon Peak skirt the water before turning north up the steep slopes.

title: Blackwolf River
body: The Blackwolf River runs out of Cragpool Lake and down through Windshear Crag to the mine at its far end, and its waters have been fouled by the Venture Company's logging of the valley. The company's crews have stripped the banks bare. Loggers, deforesters and operators work the riverside, kobold geomancers among them, oil leaks into the current, and a wagon of explosives waits nearby. Two hard bosses drive the work here: Foreman Rigger, a human, and Taskmaster Whipfang, a gnoll.

title: The Talondeep Path
body: The Talondeep Path is a long tunnel bored through the mountains, joining Windshear Crag to southern Ashenvale not far from Mystral Lake. It is a main road between Stonetalon and the forest: night elves bound for Stonetalon Peak travel it, and Horde caravans running between the mountains and Splintertree Post depend on it, so that trouble at Mystral Lake can bring them to a standstill. Deepmoss spiders lurk in its shadows and lay their eggs in the dark. Near its Stonetalon mouth waits the tauren shaman Braug Dimspirit, a sage of great wisdom who tests the seekers sent to him on their knowledge of the world's lore.

title: Stonetalon Peak
body: Stonetalon Peak crowns the far northwest of the mountains, a high forested valley that local peoples have long held sacred. Ruins of an ancient temple of Queen Azshara still stand here. The night elves keep a small outpost here with an inn and a hippogryph roost, where Keeper Albagorm watches over the land, and the Sons and Daughters of Cenarius and their botanists tend the woods, while sap beasts, twilight runners and fey dragons roam among the trees. In the Third War, Jaina Proudmoore's expedition camped by the caverns of the peak, and Thrall came there too in search of the Oracle. More recently, the druids hid Keeper Ordanus here, before spiriting him away to Ashenvale.

title: The Talon Den
body: The Talon Den is a barrow den of the druids on Stonetalon Peak. Cenarion druids and caretakers walk its halls beside the Mirkfallon dryads, and an ancient keeper of the grove, Gatekeeper Kordurus, stands among them. Here the druids keep many items of power, and to guard them they devised an intricate scheme: a gatekeeper's key hidden in a lantern at the entrance opens caches scattered through the den, and only the contents of all three can unseal the great hoard deeper within. The dryad Rynthariel holds the den's keys, and a night elf called Brother Ravenoak prowls its depths.

title: Seereth Stonebreak
body: Seereth Stonebreak is a promising shaman of the Horde, sent to Stonetalon when the land cried out. She camps where the road from the Crossroads meets the mountains, near the Greatwood Vale, and to her the spirit of Stonetalon weeps from its peaks, its rivers and its severed trees. Shamans can hear the pleas of such spirits because their magic is kin to the natural magic of the druids, she says, though many of the whispers are lost to her. One vision came clear: two man-shaped machines felling trees with impossible speed. Even so, she fears the spirits may never be soothed, and worse may follow.

title: Maggran Earthbinder
body: Maggran Earthbinder leads Sun Rock Retreat, an old tauren warrior who admits that age and countless battles have hardened his skin and his soul. He believes that is why Cairne Bloodhoof gave him this post, where gentle winds and warm sun ease his pain. Maggran takes the tauren duty as protectors of the land seriously. He holds the Bloodfury harpies of the Charred Vale to be the source of the harpies spreading across Kalimdor and wants their queen, Bloodfury Ripper, dead, and he has put a bounty on the spider Besseleth, whose fang once wounded him. With the Ripper slain, he feels his anger begin to leave him.

title: Witch Doctor Jin'Zil
body: Jin'Zil is a troll witch doctor who lives in a cave at Malaka'jin, among bubbling cauldrons. He is an old friend of Darsok Swiftdagger of the Crossroads, and he still recalls the day his friend Rokhan went off with that crazy mok'nathal Rexxar to kill the elder sister of Serena Bloodfeather, so the news of Serena's death pleases him well. His temper is gleeful and cruel. Three night elves sit caged near his camp, and for them he brews what he calls forest magic, out of sap from Stonetalon Peak, the whiskers of twilight runners, a fey dragon's scale and as many courser eyes as he can get.

title: Braelyn Firehand
body: Braelyn Firehand is a mage who camps at Sun Rock Retreat, and she despises these mountains. The druids of Stonetalon Peak and the kin of Cenarius stifle the flow of magic far beyond their forests, and here, she says, channeling a spell is like drawing water with a bucket full of holes. Her master in Jaedenar will not let her return until her work is done. That work began at the peak, among the sacred ruins of what she calls her own people's ancient temple of Azshara. When she feels magic rush back into her she exults in it, for to her life without its burning embrace is a pale mockery, and the kaldorei who spurn it are fools.

title: Keeper Albagorm
body: Keeper Albagorm watches over Stonetalon Peak for the night elves, and he mourns what greed has done to these sacred hills. When the forest spirits whisper to Faldreas Goeth'Shael in Astranaar, it is to Albagorm that the brave are sent, through the Talondeep Path and up the steep slopes past Cragpool Lake. His great hope is the Charred Vale. He means to restore it to the lush forest it once was, but first the Bloodfury harpies who bar the druids from the vale must be broken, and then the great forest spirits must be called to help, by a druid far to the south.

title: Kaela Shadowspear
body: Kaela Shadowspear is a night elf of Ashenvale, sent to Stonetalon by Sentinel Raene Wolfrunner to learn what was happening to the land, with a gnome mage assigned to accompany her. From her camp above the road into Windshear Crag she has spent most of her days fighting the Venture Company's destruction. That a night elf and a gnome must work together shows how grave things are, she admits, but she asks others not to judge Gaxim too quickly. She still misses her homeland and her friend Tara Thenysil in Astranaar, and the first time she saw the Charred Vale, she nearly wept.

title: Gaxim Rustfizzle
body: Gaxim Rustfizzle is a gnome of the Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy and Engineering Sciences, and he holds it as his duty to prove to the night elves that magic, mixtures and mechanisms together can save their forests. Swearing off magic entirely, he insists, will help no one. At Kaela Shadowspear's side he wages a cheerful war of explosions on the Venture Company, herding goblin crews with carefully placed detonations along the mountains' edges. His friends reach far: an old colleague in Tinker Town who brews volatile Nitromirglyceronium, and Collin Mauren of Stormwind's mage quarter, who works him a spell for setting off a blast from afar.

title: Ziz Fizziks
body: Ziz Fizziks was once an engineer of the Venture Company in Windshear Crag, until the company hired a gnome. The goblin was so appalled that he begged Sputtervalve of the Tinkers' Union in Ratchet for a new job, and when Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle took over the site, Ziz was thrown out. He told his man Piznik to stay behind in the mine and spy. Now he camps on the crag's western edge, eager to prove his loyalty to his new boss, though he admits a goblin's honor is only worth so much. He would happily see Gerenzo dead, and he dreams of a post in the Union's workshops in Gadgetzan or even Undermine.

title: Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle
body: Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle is the gnome who runs the Venture Company's operation in Windshear Crag, and he is not easy to look upon: his flesh seems to rot away, and he has grafted gears and metal onto his body and replaced limbs with machines. He was once one of the head engineers of Gnomeregan, working on its secret project, which ended by exploding in its makers' faces. His hiring so appalled the goblin Ziz Fizziks that he left the company, and under Gerenzo the outfit built the Super Reaper 6000, a vast woodcutting machine. From a platform high above Cragpool Lake he watches the whole site, and some in Undermine want him gone.

title: Rynthariel the Keymaster
body: Rynthariel is a dryad of the Talon Den on Stonetalon Peak, its Keymaster and, to the Horde, its leader. She sends Alliance runners across Horde lands in the Barrens, and when one of her scrolls was taken from a fallen courier and carried to Kadrak at the watch tower in the north, the Horde took it as an insult. Kadrak called her a scheming dryad and demanded more than her death: a Horde banner raised inside the den itself, so that the night elves would think twice before sending another runner through Horde territory.

title: The Spirits of Stonetalon
body: The spirits of the Stonetalon Mountains are angered, for the goblins of the Venture Company and their servants are cutting and burning the forests. The land cried out, and in Orgrimmar the far seer Zor Lonetree heard. He sent help west from the Crossroads to the promising shaman Seereth Stonebreak, who had reported deforestation on a massive scale. She asked first for the answer the goblins understand best, violence, and loggers fell in Windshear Crag. Then a vision came to her of two man-shaped machines marked XT:4 and XT:9, cutting down trees with impossible speed, and these too were destroyed, soothing many of the spirits. Yet Seereth knew it was not enough. To truly tend the spirits, the tauren elders must be consulted, and the only one she knew by name was the aged Magatha on Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff. What the Elder Crone made of the plea is another tale.

title: Cenarius' Legacy
body: Braelyn Firehand came to Stonetalon at her master's bidding, expecting nothing more than to slaughter the night elves who crawled over the ruined temple of Azshara on the peak. But the prize she was sent for had slipped away. First she wanted the flow of magic restored, and Horde blades cut down the Sons and Daughters of Cenarius and their botanists until she felt power flood back into her veins. Then her magic granted her true sight, and she found her quarry, Keeper Ordanus, hidden far off in Ashenvale. She wanted his head, and when it was brought to her she gloated over the arrogant keeper she had known long ago. Last, she revealed a secret wrung from one of the druids: how a key hidden at the entrance of the Talon Den could unlock the druids' caches, and through them the hoard within.

title: On Guard in Stonetalon
body: Sentinel Tara Thenysil of Astranaar had heard nothing from her friend Kaela Shadowspear, sent into Stonetalon with a gnome mage at her side, and she sent someone to look. Kaela was alive, camped above the road into Windshear Crag, and her companion Gaxim Rustfizzle had a plan. It began with explosions. Goblin crews were driven back while Gaxim gathered his materials: volatile Nitromirglyceronium from an old colleague in Tinker Town, made from potions brought to his door, and a scroll of messaging from Collin Mauren in Stormwind, crafted with debris from a Westfall dust devil, so that the charges could be fired from afar. With wagons of dynamite as a distraction, the Venture Company's engineering plans were stolen from the lumber mill and its letters from Windshear Mine. Kaela sent word home that the land might yet heal, and Thenysil sent the messenger on to Darnassus, where Tyrande Whisperwind herself offered her thanks.

title: Reclaiming the Charred Vale
body: In Astranaar, Faldreas Goeth'Shael listens to the spirits of the forest, and they told him of one brave enough to travel. He sent that traveler south through the Talondeep Path, across the ravaged Windshear Crag and up the steep slopes to Stonetalon Peak, where Keeper Albagorm waited. The keeper's grief was for the Charred Vale, once forest, now ash, set afire by a greedy mechanized army of industrialists. The druids wished to begin its regrowth, but the Bloodfury harpies who had settled the burned vale would not let them pass. Harpies, ambushers, slayers and roguefeathers fell until the flock was badly broken. Albagorm knew they would regroup soon, and so he sent word far south, past the Barrens and into Thousand Needles, to the druid Falfindel Waywarder at the edge of Feralas, who has the power to call great forest spirits to help in the vale's reclamation.

title: The Seeds of Gaea
body: At Sun Rock Retreat, Tammra Windfield grieves for a land wrecked by industrial greed and endless war, and she holds that only the blessings of the Earthmother can cure such an injury. Her hope lies in the Gaea seed, found nowhere else but along the shores of Mirkfallon Lake. Once the seeds were gathered, she chanted over them, imbuing them with shamanic power so that even such small kernels of life might bloom. They were then carried west into the heart of the destruction, the Charred Vale, past harpies and raging fire spirits, and planted in mounds of fertile soil. Such seeds resist corruption, Tammra says, and will make a foothold for other life. In time the Venture Company will pack up its saws, the fire spirits will calm, the harpies will be pushed out by the land itself, and only then will Stonetalon truly know peace.

title: Gerenzo's Orders
body: When the Venture Company hired the gnome Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle to run its Windshear Crag outfit, the goblin engineer Ziz Fizziks was so appalled he begged Sputtervalve of the Tinkers' Union for a new job, and was soon thrown out. His man Piznik, sent down to the mines, stayed behind to spy. While patrols closed in, Piznik dug out a sample of the gold-green ore Gerenzo had ordered mined in bulk, then slipped away himself, and Ziz meant to send it to the engineers of Undermine, keeping a piece for himself. Next came the blueprints of the Super Reaper 6000, Gerenzo's monstrous woodcutter, taken from a company operator and sealed with stolen documents for Sputtervalve in Ratchet. Sputtervalve answered with orders from higher up: the trade princes disapproved of Razdunk's dealings with the gnome, and Director Riddlevox wanted Gerenzo removed. Gerenzo, once a head engineer of Gnomeregan, was slain on his platform above Cragpool Lake, and his mechanical arm carried back as proof.

title: The Fall of Camp Aparaje
body: Makaba Flathoof waits at the edge of the mountains by the Barrens, one of the very few who lived through the day the Grimtotem came to Camp Aparaje. He killed all he could before he fled, and now he asks only that more of them die: ruffians and mercenaries in the woods to the west, then the brutes of Grundig Darkcloud, who led the raid, at Grimtotem Post. Inside the post waited something Makaba never expected. His daughter Kaya, believed lost in the attack, was alive and a prisoner. Freed, she begged to be taken back to Camp Aparaje before her captors noticed, and Grimtotem brutes, ruffians and sorcerers struck again along the way. From the ruins of her village she knew the road home. Makaba sent the good news on to Sun Rock Retreat, to Kaya's aunt Tammra Windfield, who could scarcely believe her niece still lived.

title: Earthen Arise
body: The shaman Mor'rogal of Sun Rock Retreat could feel a tension in the air of Stonetalon, a sense that something evil lurked beneath the mountains. Southeast of the retreat, in a deep cave in Boulderslide Ravine, the Gogger kobolds were mining a rare crystal called resonite in a frenzy, and Mor'rogal wanted samples and word of what lay at the cave's bottom. He half remembered a legend tied to resonite, and the crystals confirmed it: they bore a trace of earthen magic. The earthen were made by the titans to shape the very land, and at the bottom of the cave stood a resonite cask in which one of them, Goggeroc, lay sleeping. Mor'rogal feared what such a being might mean for all of Kalimdor. He enchanted a crystal to break the cask, knowing the earthen would be weak from his long slumber, and Goggeroc was slain while that weakness lasted.
